messages:
maya: Heads-up: p95 for /chat/stream (prod, tier-B) drifted to ~210ms over the last 10m. Spike correlates with KV cache miss bursts + long-seq requests.
carla: I pulled a sample trace and profiled it. Pattern: KV miss -> larger microbatch formation -> kernel switchover stalls. Putting a quick sim together to test token-target change.
carla: ```json
sim:{
  "route": "/chat/stream",
  "route_tier": "B",
  "token_target_algo": "slo_dyn_v2",
  "params": {"base": 32, "alpha": 0.6, "max": 128}
}
```
marek: If we reduce per-request token_budget we shrink microbatches -> fewer kernel switchover events and lower p95. Tradeoff: throughput loss. How much throughput regression is acceptable?
sam: Proposal: closed-loop p95-driven token target. Simple control law: target = clamp(base + k*(p95_target - measured_p95), min, max) with 60s EWMA smoothing. Start conservative.
dan: Also watch kernel selection overhead. In perf lab, prefetching kernels for the predicted next seq length reduced switchover by ~15ms. If we change batch sizes often, prefetch helps.
erin: Canary plan suggestion: sim -> 1% prod -> 5% prod. Metrics to monitor: p95, throughput (rps), error rate, avg_kernel_switch_ms, avg_batch_tokens, kv_miss_ratio. I can own the alerts and automated rollback conditions.
maya: Also add a queue policy tweak: when a request arrives and remaining token budget for batch is low, prefer adding smaller/older requests to avoid head-of-line blocking from long seq requests.
sam: I opened a config PR with the slo_dyn_v2 params and queue policy change: https://git.internal/r/slo/slo_dyn_v2 (link). Ready for canary. Rollback conditions: p95 > target OR throughput drop > 8%.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout started for slo_dyn_v2 -> 1% traffic on tier-B routes.
carla: Adding perf counters to traces: kv_miss_ratio, avg_batch_tokens, kernel_switch_ms. Dan, can you run an overnight perf scan on canary cluster and include kernel scheduling counters?
dan: On it. Scheduled run for 03:15 UTC tomorrow. Will post the CSV + flamegraphs.
maya: :thumbsup: thanks team, please keep notes in the canary thread and tag @erin for any automated alarms.
erin: I'll attach the alerting dashboards and add the rollback runbook to the canary PR.
carla: After the sim tests: p95 dropped from 210ms -> 160ms with slo_dyn_v2 but throughput down ~7% and small increase in kv_miss_ratio. That's within expected tradeoffs; canary will validate real traffic shape.
marek: Good enough as starting point. If kernel prefetch reduces switch_ms further we can recover throughput.
sam: If canary looks stable after 24h at 5% we can incrementally roll to 25% with the same checks.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary progressed to 5% after automated health checks passed (first stage).
